name: Safe corridors for temporary distal-femur spanning external fixation
region: femoral shaft, knee, and tibial shaft
corridor: Anterior-to-lateral femoral shaft and anteromedial tibial shaft percutaneous pin corridors

positioning.text: Position supine with the entire injured limb accessible and imageable from proximal femur through tibia.

setup.text: Map soft-tissue injury and future plate or nail paths first; place femoral pins in the proximal third and tibial pins in midshaft when later conversion is anticipated.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark femoral shaft, quadriceps envelope, patella, fibular head, tibial crest, and planned definitive incisions.

incision.text: Use adequate small incisions for blunt dissection to bone rather than driving pins directly through tethered skin.

superficial_interval.text: Femoral pins pass through anterior rectus split or direct lateral vastus; tibial pins begin about 1 cm medial to the crest on the anteromedial surface.

deep_interval.text: Advance drill guides to bone, drill bicortically without plunging, and keep the tibial trajectory approximately 20 degrees from sagittal away from posterolateral structures.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, quadriceps or vastus lateralis to femur; skin and subcutaneous tissue directly to anteromedial tibia.

structures_encountered.text: Rectus femoris or vastus lateralis, femoral cortex, tibial crest, and anteromedial tibial cortex are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Sciatic nerve, femoral and popliteal vessels, common and deep peroneal nerves, anterior tibial vessels, saphenous nerve, and future surgical planes are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid medial/posterior femoral trajectories, the fibular-head peroneal-nerve zone, and posterolateral tibial drilling toward the anterior tibial bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid soft-tissue tethering around pins and thermal or plunge injury during drilling; use sleeves, irrigation, and controlled bicortical depth.

exposure.text: Provides safe percutaneous skeletal purchase for a knee-spanning frame while keeping traumatized and definitive operative zones clear.

limitations.text: Safe zones are corridor guides, not substitutes for patient-specific imaging, palpation, soft-tissue assessment, or direct technique.

extensions.text: Add pins only after remapping neurovascular and definitive implant corridors; do not crowd the future operative field.

indications.text: Use for staged temporary stabilization of unstable distal-femur injuries with soft-tissue compromise or physiologic need for damage control.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid crushed, infected, burned, or planned-incision skin and any corridor whose anatomy cannot be confidently defined.

implant_implications.text: Keep pins outside the future nail path and plate footprint and sufficiently distant from fracture and definitive incisions.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm bicortical purchase, pin trajectory, joint clearance, and frame alignment without drill plunge.

closure.text: Release tethered skin around each pin, dress pin sites, and document neurovascular status after frame assembly.

complications.text: Complications include neurovascular injury, pin-track infection, thermal necrosis, fracture propagation, joint penetration, stiffness, and contamination of definitive fixation corridors.

bailouts.text: If the safe corridor or future plan is uncertain, stop and relocate under imaging or direct exposure rather than accept a hazardous pin.

procedure_applications.condition: Temporary knee-spanning fixation is required while preserving future definitive surgical corridors

questions.question: What is the safest femoral arc?
Where should tibial pins begin?
questions.answer: About 1 cm medial to the tibial crest on the anteromedial surface.

questions.question: Why keep pins away from future fixation?
questions.answer: To avoid contaminating or obstructing definitive plate or nail corridors.
